purpose.is: Turns the owner's build-mode rule and the owner's hold into flags the system reads: entity flag:build_mode (on or off, scope, expiry the system enforces, card id) and entity flag:hold (on or off, and the owner word the hold lamp waits on).

N-44 is the single writer of both entities. N-29 decides (one ruling per card, typed effects); N-44 applies; N-42 draws the hold lamp and re-enters through N-29; N-03, N-07 and N-09 read. No other node, script or seat writes a flag row (review NF-A9).

While build mode is on, old-line gates, hooks, guards, leases, watches and status rules are not rendered into seats in scope (N-13), and a refusal that names an old rule is recorded as rule.bit and does not stop the ticket (factory-rebuild-plan.xml failure case governance-interference).
purpose.is-not: It is not a bypass of the gate: coq/gate on the head sha (N-08, N-25) and the reviewer record (N-19) still decide a merge under build mode. It is not a lift of permissions for the owner's break glass, which is N-42's one-time control.action. Flag:freeze is not a control flag: N-51 writes it in the exit verdict's own transaction.
purpose.why: L11 F1: build mode is a note, not a mechanism, and an agent switching rules off by hand is the pattern the owner rejected the same day. herdr/config/exemptions.json already has the right shape: rule, until, card_id, why (L11 section 8). Review NF-A9: three volumes named three writers of flag:hold.

input.record: A ruling whose effects array carries a typed flag effect (record.schema.json#/$defs/flag_effect): build-mode.set with state, scope, expires_at and card_id (state off turns build mode off early); control.halt (USERHALT) or control.resume (USERGO) with card_id. A Controls screen action re-enters through N-29 and arrives here as a ruling.
A restore started a new epoch (shared/contracts.xml#restore); package flags runs inside that first Commit (mechanism step 6) and the record is the evidence it did.
The scheduler tick; on every tick the node compares now with the live build-mode expiry.
Expiry reconcile before the first dispatch.

output.record: Build mode as the system now holds it: on or off, scope, expires_at, card id, the ruling id, flag_version and a reason (ruling, extend, ended-early, expired, start-reconcile, restore).
A ruling refused on validation: expiry in the past, expiry beyond flags.build_mode.max_duration, or a scope not in the enum.
The compare-and-swap lost twice (reason race); the live state is unchanged.
The ruling did not come from an owner principal on the owner page, the owner CLI or the Controls screen (reason not-owner); nothing changes.
flag:hold set or cleared: state, waits_on (USERGO or GOFACTORY), reason (userhalt, usergo, restore, bootstrap), card and ruling ids.
control.resume before bootstrap B7 (reason not-ready, the missing proofs named); the hold stays.
A hold effect from anything but an owner principal (reason not-owner).
output.reads: N-07 (copies flag:build_mode and its version into the dispatch as contracts.schema.json#/$defs/build_mode; refuses GrantDispatch under hold), N-13 (renders the seat bundle from that copy), N-03 and N-09 (read flag:hold every tick), N-42 (the hold lamp and the build-mode lamp; turn-off control), N-28 (one card when build mode expires with rebuild tickets still open), N-51 (the exit test records both states of the day).

authority.rule: A flag effect is applied only when the ruling's server-derived principal (shared/authority.xml#role-derivation) is the owner and its source is the owner page, the owner CLI or the Controls screen of the owner page. A ruling from a relay, a policy, an import or a seat never changes a flag; N-44 writes 403 not-owner and N-29's card stays open (shared/authority.xml#relayable-rulings allows a relay only none and ticket.unblock).

USERHALT and USERGO are owner words (shared/authority.xml#owner-words): N-29 matches them; N-44 never reads message text. control.resume clears the hold only at bootstrap B7 or later (shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap); before B7 it is hold.state 412 not-ready naming the missing proofs.
A restore sets the hold with no ruling (the store itself decides, shared/contracts.xml#restore); only an owner ruling clears it.

mechanism.where: Go package flags inside the service, the only code path that writes entity flag:build_mode or flag:hold; every write is one Store.Commit (shared/contracts.xml#batch) with a compare-and-swap on the entity version and the record in the same transaction; operation keys N-44/flag.set/<ruling_id>/r1, N-44/flag.expire/build_mode@<version>/r1 and N-44/flag.hold/restore@<epoch>/r1 (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys).
mechanism.step: On a ruling: check authority (section authority); for each flag effect in order, validate. build-mode.set on: expires_at after now, at most flags.build_mode.max_duration (default P7D) ahead, scope in the enum. build-mode.set off: valid in any state (ended-early). control.halt: always valid. control.resume: bootstrap:state is B7 or B8.

Commit the entity write and the state record together. A replay of the same ruling returns the first reply (same operation key, same request hash); N-29's one ruling per card means a card answered twice never reaches here twice. On 409 version, re-read and re-validate once; a second 409 is build-mode.state 409 reason race.
On every tick: if build mode is on and now is at or after expires_at, commit off with reason expired, card_id of the ruling it closes.
On unit.start: run step 3 once before the first dispatch, so a build mode that expired while the service was down is cleared before any seat renders.

When build mode turns off by expiry and N-03 reports rebuild tickets still open (waiting, ready or in_flight with scope rebuild), set open_rebuild_tickets; N-28 turns it into one owner card (extend or let the rules apply), which carries no default.

Restore (shared/contracts.xml#restore step 2): the restore's first Commit calls package flags inside its own transaction (Store.Do), so flag:hold on (waits_on USERGO, reason restore), build mode off (reason restore) and both state records are written by this node's code in the restore transaction itself; no dispatch can fall between the new epoch and the hold. Restore code never writes a flag entity directly.
mechanism.scope: Scope rebuild applies to tickets whose lane is rebuild (cut from this spec book by N-17 and N-18); product to product-lane tickets; all to every ticket. A ticket's scope is fixed at cut and read by N-13 from the dispatch record.

diagram.mermaid: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> off off --> on : build-mode.set on (owner principal) CAS ok on --> on : build-mode.set on, later expiry (extend) on --> off : build-mode.set off (ended-early) on --> off : tick at or after expires_at (system) on --> off : store.restored off --> off : expired-at-start reconcile (unit.start)

effects.effect: With build mode on and the ticket in scope, the seat bundle omits every hook, guard and watch from the old line (compaction-guard binding, nudge, trust writer, idle watch, prettier PostToolUse, AutoMem) and renders settings from the role only; the bundle hash records build_mode and scope.

A failure record whose reason names an old rule (the old-rule table of shared/principles.xml#build-mode) is written as rule.bit 300 with the rule name, and the attempt is not charged; one fix ticket request per rule name goes to N-03.
Under flag:hold, GrantDispatch and work-class leases are refused; maintenance leases are allowed (shared/contracts.xml#lease-machine).
rule.bit is not a card; the expiry-with-open-tickets record is one card.
The hold lamp (HOLD and the owner word it waits on) and the build-mode lamp (on, scope, time left) with turn off now, which re-enters at N-29.
Build mode changes nothing: the gate, the reviewer record and the machine merge apply; a rule that blocks a rebuild ticket is a defect in the rule, a failing test is not.

start.s: The ruling arrives as a record from N-29 (the owner's card answer on the owner page, the owner CLI, or a Controls screen action). No agent edits a flag file; no seat reads a memory note.
Expiry is enforced by the tick (N-06) and reconciled at unit start; a restore holds by itself; no one has to remember to turn anything off.

wait.fallback: one re-read and retry; then build-mode.state 409 reason race; the live state is unchanged and the next tick re-evaluates
the system turns it off and posts one card if rebuild tickets remain open

wait.what: N-03 open-ticket count for the expiry card
wait.fallback: post the card with count unknown rather than skip it

wait.what: the owner word that clears a hold
wait.timeout: none; the hold lamp shows which word it waits on
wait.fallback: nothing dispatches; ticks, health, backups, the poll and push keep running; the owner card carries no default and no deadline (shared/authority.xml#owner-words)

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a human remembering to turn build mode off. The expiry removes that cog; the owner's only action is optional (extend or end early). The hold is meant to wait for the owner, and the lamp says so.

retries.recover: After three failures the node writes build-mode.state 409 race and leaves the live state; readers read the entity, not the attempt.
retries.report: A ruling refused for an expiry beyond the maximum is 422 and goes back to N-29, which re-asks with the maximum stated; never silently clipped.

many-agents.readers: Sixteen seats rendering at once read build mode from the dispatch record N-07 gave them (N-07 copies the entity and its version in the GrantDispatch transaction), so a flip during a render cannot split one seat's bundle between two states.
many-agents.writers: Only package flags writes the two entities, by compare-and-swap; rulings are applied in store sequence order, so two rulings in the same second resolve deterministically and the later one wins.
many-agents.collision: An expiry tick and an extend ruling at the same moment: both CAS on the same version; one wins; the loser re-reads. If extend won, build mode stays on with the later expiry; if expiry won, the extend applies on its retry as a fresh on.
USERHALT and a restore at once: both set the hold; the second CAS re-reads, finds it on, and keeps the stronger waits_on (USERGO); one lamp.
A seat whose bundle was rendered under on while build mode turned off keeps its bundle for that run (one-shot, D02); the next attempt renders under the new state.

status-codes.emits: Applied (on, off, extend, ended-early, expired, restore); system acts; with open_rebuild_tickets greater than 0 on an expiry, the owner acts through one card.
Ruling invalid (bad expiry, bad scope); N-29 acts by re-asking with the reason.
CAS lost twice (race); system acts (next tick).
Not an owner principal; nobody acts (the card stays open).
Hold set or cleared; N-03, N-07, N-09 act on the next tick; the hold lamp follows.
USERGO before bootstrap B7; the owner reads the missing proofs on the hold lamp's card.
Not an owner principal; nobody acts.
Written by N-11 on this node's rule; listed here because build mode defines when it may be written.

state-paths.path: Flag transitions as log lines; the store is the truth.
state-paths.rule: herdr/config/exemptions.json is not written by this node; it is a source and is retired with the herdr config tree by N-49 once N-13 renders bundles from the flag.

edges.out: build-mode.state (through the dispatch record of N-07)
build-mode.state and hold.state (the lamps and the turn-off control)

item.check: An owner ruling turns build mode on with its expiry and card id.
item.proof: A test ruling from an owner principal on the owner page; one build-mode.state 200 on with the same card_id and expires_at; entity flag:build_mode version bumped.

item.check: build-mode.set off ends build mode early.
item.proof: A ruling with state off while on; build-mode.state 200 off reason ended-early.

item.check: A relayed or seat-produced ruling changes no flag.
item.proof: A ruling with source relay and one whose principal is a seat; build-mode.state 403 not-owner and hold.state 403 not-owner; entity versions unchanged.

item.check: The system turns build mode off at expiry without any ruling.
item.proof: Fake clock advanced past expires_at; one build-mode.state 200 off reason expired by N-44.

item.check: An expired build mode is cleared at unit start.
item.proof: Store seeded with an expired on; unit start; off record before the first dispatch record.

item.check: USERGO before B7 is refused and the hold stays.
item.proof: bootstrap:state B4; a control.resume ruling; hold.state 412 not-ready listing the missing proofs; flag:hold still on.
A test restore; the first Commit's seqs hold store.restored, hold.state 200 on waits_on USERGO and build-mode.state 200 off reason restore, all in one epoch-opening transaction.

item.check: No other node writes a flag.
item.proof: The statements registry (shared/contracts.xml#statements) lists flag:hold and flag:build_mode writes for N-44 only; a Commit touching either entity from another principal is 403 kind_not_permitted.

item.check: A rule refusal under build mode does not charge an attempt.
item.proof: N-11 test: failure record naming an old rule; rule.bit 300 written; attempt unchanged; one fix ticket request.

may.do: turn build mode on, extend it or end it, and set or clear the hold, through a card answer on the owner page, the owner CLI or the Controls screen
apply owner rulings, expire build mode, hold on restore, write build-mode.state, hold.state and rule.bit

may-not.do: set or clear any flag; a chat relay carries only none and ticket.unblock
write build-mode.state, hold.state, rule.bit or any flag; read build mode from anywhere but its dispatch record
turn a flag on by editing a file, a memory note or a config

1 or 0, with the owner word it waits on as a label.
How often each old rule bit; the top rule is the next fix ticket.
monitoring.lamp: Lit while flag:hold is on: HOLD and the owner word it waits on.

step.when: a rebuild ticket is refused by an old rule

runbook.step: Nothing by hand. Read the rule.bit record and the fix ticket request; the ticket re-dispatched on its own.
Answer the card on the owner page: extend (a new ruling with a new expiry) or let the rules apply.

step.when: the owner is away from the page

runbook.step: The owner CLI is the other owner surface; a chat relay never sets a flag, and nothing edits the store by hand.
runbook.cold-start: The flag rows are in the store; unit start reconciles expiry; nothing else to restore.

sources.source: Principle build-mode: old rules off for rebuild tickets, nodes ship dark, a blocking rule is a defect, the ledger records which rule bit
Case governance-interference: proceed, cut the fix ticket, record which rule bit
D13 B: build mode as a flag with an expiry that the gates read, the shape of herdr/config/exemptions.json
F1 build mode is a note, not a mechanism
Exemptions with an expiry and a card id as the shape of a build-mode switch
The owner's words and the four statements

reject.source: herdr/config/exemptions.json as the live flag file
reject.reason: A file an agent edits is a hand step and lives in the repository; the flag is a store entity with a ruling behind it. The file's shape is kept, its role is not.
An open-ended exemption is how the old rules stayed half-on; the owner's D13 ruling names the expiry.

reject.source: build mode lifting the gate or the reviewer
reject.reason: The owner's statement is about old governance rules, not tests; D15 keeps the machine verdict for every merge.

reject.source: build mode or a hold set from a chat relay (book 1.0.0 runbook break glass)
reject.reason: A relay is not the owner principal; owner words and flag effects come only from the owner page or CLI (shared/authority.xml#owner-words).

reject.source: N-29 or N-42 writing flag:hold directly (book 1.0.0, three writers)
reject.reason: Three writers of one row race and disagree on the lamp; N-29 decides, N-44 writes (review NF-A9).
Dead enforcement files referenced by no settings (L11 section 9); under build mode and the repo-owned seat layer they are not loaded; N-49 disposes of them.

shared-needs.need: principles.xml#build-mode with the old-rule table: every old-line rule name and the refusal string it prints, so N-11 can match a refusal to a rule.
flags (state-store.xml#flags): entities flag:build_mode and flag:hold, owner N-44, the only writer; the statement text that names N-29 or N-42 as a writer of flag:hold changes to N-44.
contracts.schema.json#/$defs/build_mode is the dispatch copy; N-29's $defs/effect should $ref this node's record.schema.json#/$defs/flag_effect for build-mode.set, control.halt and control.resume.
